definition_zh: 不同地；相异地；以不同的方式
definition_en: in a way that is not the same as another way
core_image: 两条岔开的小路：同一件事走出两种走法
scene: 老师说每个人解题的思路都可以不一样。Everyone solves the maths problem differently, and that is okay.
sceneCN: 这里 differently 是「不同地」（第 1 个义项：方式不一样）；句意是每个人解题方式都不同，这没关系。

derivatives.zh: different 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「不同的」的副词形式
different 加名词后缀 -ence 构成，义为「差异；不同」
同源动词，义为「不同；相异」
加前缀 in-（不），义为「漠不关心的」

senses.title: In a way that is not the same
senses.definition: in a manner that is not the same as something else
senses.definitionCN: 以与别的方式不一样的方式
senses.example: We all learn differently, so find your own way to study.
senses.exampleCN: 我们学习方式各不相同，所以要找到适合自己的方法。
senses.why: The suffix -ly turns the adjective different into a manner word, so the core image is two paths that split apart.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词 different 变成方式词，核心意象是两条岔开的小路。

senses.title: In a changed manner
senses.titleCN: 换了方式地；改变做法地
senses.definition: in a way that is not the usual or old way
senses.definitionCN: 用不同于以往、不同于习惯的方式
senses.example: After the lesson, I began to think about failure differently.
senses.exampleCN: 上完这节课后，我开始用不同的眼光看待失败。
senses.why: When a manner word points away from the old habit, it means the path has turned, so it also covers changed ways.
senses.whyCN: 方式词一旦离开旧习惯，就说明路转向了，所以它也能表示改变后的做法。

intro.en: Differently comes from the Latin family of differ.
intro.cn: differently 来自 differ 的拉丁语词族。

items.en: The verb differre meant to carry apart or to disagree, built on dis- (apart) and ferre (to carry).
items.cn: 拉丁语 differre 意为分开携带、不一致，由 dis-（分开）加 ferre（携带）构成。

items.en: Old French had differer, keeping the sense of being unlike.
items.cn: 古法语有 differer，保留了「不一样」的意思。

items.en: English took the adjective different from this family in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪，英语从这个词族吸收了形容词 different。

items.en: The manner suffix -ly was added to build the adverb.
items.cn: 人们给它加上方式后缀 -ly，构成副词。

items.en: Differently is now the standard way to say a thing is done in another manner.
items.cn: 如今 differently 是表示「换个方式做」的标准说法。

note.en: These words sit around the differ family and its sound pattern.
note.cn: 这些词围绕 differ 词族及其读音模式。

definition_zh: 困难的；艰难的；难对付的；不易相处的
definition_en: hard to do, understand, or deal with
core_image: 一座爬不上去的陡坡，每一步都要用力
scene: 数学考试最后一道题，全班只有一个人做出来。The last question was too difficult for most of us, so we left it blank.
sceneCN: 这里 difficult 是「困难的」（第 1 个义项：难以完成）；句意是最后一题对我们大多数人来说太难，只好空着。

derivatives.zh: difficult 加名词后缀 -y 构成，义为「困难；难题」
difficult 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「困难地」

senses.title: Hard to do or understand
senses.definition: needing much effort or skill to do, understand, or answer
senses.definitionCN: 需要很大努力或技巧才能完成、理解或回答
senses.example: This puzzle is difficult, but I will not give up.
senses.exampleCN: 这道谜题很难，但我不会放弃。
senses.why: The Latin root ficultas carries the idea of effort and even trickery, so the word paints a task that pushes back against you.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根带有「费力」甚至「刁难」的意思，所以这个词描绘的是会「顶回来」的任务。

senses.title: Hard to deal with
senses.definition: not easy to get along with or to manage
senses.definitionCN: 不容易相处或应付
senses.example: My cousin can be difficult when he is hungry.
senses.exampleCN: 我表弟饿的时候挺难对付的。
senses.why: A person can push back just like a hard task, so the image of resistance moved from work to people.
senses.whyCN: 人会像难题一样「顶人」，抵抗的画面便从事情转移到了人身上。

senses.title: Full of trouble
senses.definition: full of problems or worry
senses.definitionCN: 充满问题或忧虑
senses.example: It was a difficult year for our family, but we stayed together.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年我们家过得很艰难，但我们一直在一起。
senses.why: When every step costs effort and the road stays steep, life itself is called difficult.
senses.whyCN: 当每一步都费劲、坡一直很陡时，生活本身也被称作 difficult。

intro.en: Difficult is built on Latin parts about effort and trickery.
intro.cn: difficult 由拉丁语中表示费力、刁难的成分构成。

items.en: The root dificultas came from difficilis, meaning not easy, built on dis- (not) and facilis (easy to do).
items.cn: 拉丁语 dificultas 出自 difficilis（不容易），由 dis-（不）加 facilis（容易做的）构成。

items.en: Facilis itself came from facere, to make or to do.
items.cn: facilis 又来自动词 facere（做、制作）。

items.en: Middle English borrowed difficult from Old French and Latin around the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 约在十五世纪，中古英语经古法语从拉丁语借入 difficult。

items.en: At first it often meant hard to please or stubborn about people.
items.cn: 最初它常指人难讨好、执拗。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the hard-task sense and the hard-person sense.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留「难事」和「难对付的人」两个义项。

note.en: These words share the hard-task field or the sound of difficult.
note.cn: 这些词属于难事义场，或与 difficult 读音相近。

definition_en: the state of being hard, or a hard problem
core_image: 一块搬不动的大石头挡在路上
scene: 搬新家那天，客厅的旧沙发卡在楼梯口。We had difficulty moving the old sofa down the stairs.
sceneCN: 这里 difficulty 是「费力、困难」（第 1 个义项：做起来吃力）；句意是我们搬旧沙发下楼很吃力。

derivatives.zh: difficulty 的形容词形式，义为「困难的」

senses.title: The state of being hard
senses.definition: the fact that something needs much effort
senses.definitionCN: 某事需要很大努力的情况
senses.example: She read the long English story without much difficulty.
senses.exampleCN: 她毫不费力地读完了那个长长的英语故事。
senses.why: The Latin ending -tas names a state, so difficulty is the name of the pushing-back feeling you meet in a hard task.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语后缀 -tas 表示状态，difficulty 便给难事带来的「顶劲」起了名字。

senses.title: A hard problem or trouble
senses.definition: something hard to deal with, or a problem
senses.definitionCN: 难以处理的事情或麻烦
senses.example: The map had one difficulty: it did not show the small bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这张地图有个问题：没标出那座小桥。
senses.why: A state of being hard soon becomes a thing you can point at, so the word names each single hard spot.
senses.whyCN: 「难」的状态很快变成可以指认的东西，于是这个词也能指一个个具体的难点。

senses.title: Money trouble or trouble in life
senses.definition: problems with money or with life
senses.definitionCN: 钱或生活上的难处
senses.example: His family had difficulty paying the school fees last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年他家交学费有困难。
senses.why: Hard states in daily life usually start with money, so the word reached into bills and debts.
senses.whyCN: 生活里的难处多半从钱开始，这个词便延伸到账单与欠债上。

items.en: The word was built on dis- (not) plus facilis (easy), from facere (to do).

items.en: Old French carried difficulte into medieval Europe.

items.en: English took it in the fourteenth century as difficulte, then difficulty.

items.en: The plural difficulties names every hard spot one by one.
items.cn: 复数 difficulties 把一个个难点逐一指名。

definition_en: the main meal of the day, or a formal evening meal
core_image: 一天中摆得最满的那张餐桌
scene: 傍晚六点，厨房飘出红烧肉的香味。The whole family sits together for dinner at six every evening.
sceneCN: 这里 dinner 是「正餐、晚餐」（第 1 个义项：一天的主餐）；句意是全家每晚六点一起吃晚饭。

senses.title: The main meal of the day
senses.definition: the biggest meal eaten in the day
senses.definitionCN: 一天中吃得最多的一餐
senses.example: We have dinner together when Dad comes home.
senses.exampleCN: 爸爸回家后我们一起吃正餐。
senses.why: The old French word disner meant to break the fast, and the big meal earned the name.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 disner 意为「开斋、进食」，一天中最丰盛的一餐便得了这个名字。

senses.title: A formal evening meal
senses.definition: a special or formal meal in the evening

senses.example: The school held a dinner for the winning team.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为夺冠的队伍举办了一场晚宴。
senses.why: When the main meal moved to evening and got dressed up, it became an event with speeches and toasts.
senses.whyCN: 当主餐挪到晚上并变得隆重，它就成了有致辞、有举杯的宴会。

intro.en: Dinner began as a French verb about eating.
intro.cn: dinner 起源于一个表示「进食」的法语动词。

items.en: Old French disner meant to dine, to take the first food of the day.
items.cn: 古法语 disner 意为进餐，即吃一天的第一顿。

items.en: Earlier forms like desjunare meant to un-fast, to break the night's fast.
items.cn: 更早的形式如 desjunare 意为「解除斋戒」，即结束一夜未食。

items.en: English took diner around the thirteenth century, later spelled dinner.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语借入 diner，后拼写定为 dinner。

items.en: The word moved from the first meal to the biggest meal of the day.
items.cn: 词义从一天的第一餐转指一天中最大的一餐。

items.en: In Britain dinner is often the evening meal; in some places it is the noon meal.
items.cn: 在英国 dinner 常指晚餐；有些地方则指中午的主餐。

note.en: These are meal words that stand next to dinner.
note.cn: 这些是与 dinner 相邻的用餐词。

senses.title: Straight, without bending or stopping
senses.definition: going straight from one place to another, or with nothing in between

senses.example: There is a direct bus from our school to the museum.

senses.why: The Latin root means arranged in a line, so the core image is an unbent line between two points.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「排成直线」，核心意象是两点之间一条不弯的线。

senses.title: To guide or lead
senses.definition: to tell people what to do, or to lead an activity

senses.example: The music teacher will direct the school choir this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年将由音乐老师指挥校合唱团。
senses.why: A straight line needs a starting hand, so making things go straight became leading them.
senses.whyCN: 直线需要一个起点，让事物走直线便变成了「引导」。

senses.title: To aim at a target
senses.definition: to point something at a person or place

sensesIntro.en: Dirty starts with unclean things, then rude acts, then the verb.
sensesIntro.cn: dirty 先指不干净的事物，再指粗俗卑劣的行为，最后作动词表示弄脏。

latinIntro.en: The family root is Old English drit, mud.
latinIntro.cn: 词族核心是古英语 drit（泥浆）。

definition_zh: 使丧失能力；使伤残；（技术）使失效；使停用
definition_en: to make someone unable to do something, or to stop a machine working
core_image: 一只手按下开关，机器停止转动
scene: 机房设备维护课上，老师演示操作。Remember to disable the alarm before you open the door.
sceneCN: 这里 disable 是「使失效、停用」（第 2 个义项：让设备停止工作）；句意是开门前记得先解除警报。

derivatives.zh: disable 的词基，义为「能力」
过去分词作形容词，义为「残疾的；失效的」
反构词，义为「使能够」
disable 加名词后缀构成，义为「残疾；功能障碍」

senses.title: To make someone unable
senses.definition: to hurt someone so that part of their body or mind cannot work normally
senses.definitionCN: 使身体或心智的一部分无法正常工作
senses.example: The illness disabled his left leg for months.
senses.exampleCN: 那场病让他的左腿几个月不能活动。
senses.why: Able means can do; the prefix dis- takes the power away, so disable is to un-able someone.
senses.whyCN: able 表示「能够」，前缀 dis- 把能力拿走，disable 即「使失去能力」。

senses.title: To stop a machine or system
senses.definition: to switch off or break a device so it cannot work
senses.definitionCN: 关掉或破坏设备使其无法运转
senses.example: The virus disabled the whole computer system.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒使整个计算机系统瘫痪了。
senses.why: A machine is able to work; disabling it is removing that ability too.
senses.whyCN: 机器有运转的能力，disable 同样是把这个能力移除。

intro.en: Disable is the prefix dis- on the old verb abide.
intro.cn: disable 是前缀 dis- 加在古动词 abide 上构成的。

items.en: Old French abler meant to make able, from Latin habilis (easy to handle).
items.cn: 古法语 abler 意为使能够，出自拉丁语 habilis（易于掌握的）。

items.en: English formed ablen, to make able.
items.cn: 中古英语构成 ablen，意为使能够。

items.en: Adding dis- (apart, away) built disable in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪加上 dis-（离开、除去）构成 disable。

items.en: First it meant to weaken legally or physically.
items.cn: 最初指在法律或身体上削弱。

items.en: Modern use covers injuries, and switching off machines and programmes.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖身体伤残以及关闭机器与程序。

note.en: These words share the able root or the dis- prefix.
note.cn: 这些词同出 able 词根，或带 dis- 前缀。

entries.definition: noun: the state of being unable

normalIntro.en: Split the word: dis- (away) + able (can do).
normalIntro.cn: 拆开单词：dis-（除去）+ able（能够）。

normal.en: disable = dis + able, take the ability away.
normal.cn: disable = dis + able，把能力拿走。

normal.en: enable is the opposite: give the ability.
normal.cn: enable 是反义词：赋予能力。

normal.en: the disabled means disabled people as a group.
normal.cn: the disabled 指残疾人群体。

normal.en: disable the alarm means switch it off.
normal.cn: disable the alarm 意思是关掉警报。

normal.en: remember abil- hides inside: ability, disable, enable.
normal.cn: 注意 abil- 藏在 ability、disable、enable 里面。

abstract.en: Picture a power plug pulled out of the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象电源插头被从墙上拔下。

abstract.en: Feel a hand press the big red stop button.
abstract.cn: 体会手按下红色大停止键的感觉。

abstract.en: See a robot freeze in the middle of a step.
abstract.cn: 想象机器人走到一半突然定格。

examples.en: The security guard disabled the alarm before checking the hall.
examples.cn: 保安在检查大厅前先解除了警报。

examples.en: A heavy rain disabled the traffic lights on our street.
examples.cn: 一场大雨使我们街上的红绿灯失灵了。

examples.en: Grandpa's eyes were disabled by the illness, so we read news for him.
examples.cn: 爷爷的眼睛因病失明，我们便读新闻给他听。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弟斯诶波」——弟弟撕掉了电池（battery），机器立刻失去能力

root: 来自中古英语 disable，dis-（除去）+ ablen（使能够）；ablen 出自古法语 abler，源于拉丁语 habilis（易于掌握的）。

sensesIntro.en: Disable removes ability from a body or a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: disable 表示把能力从人或机器身上移除。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pulling out the power plug
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手拔掉电源插头

branches.en: A body that cannot work normally
One verb, two kinds of ability

branches.cn: 被关闭的警报、系统与功能
伤残之后的帮助与照顾

intro.en: Disable wears its meaning on the outside: dis- + able.
intro.cn: disable 的意思写在字面上：dis- + able。

latinIntro.en: The able root goes back to Latin habilis, easy to handle.
latinIntro.cn: able 词根可追溯到拉丁语 habilis（易于掌握的）。

definition_zh: 不利条件；劣势；缺点；损害
definition_en: an unfavourable condition, or something that causes problems
core_image: 赛跑时比别人多背一个沉重的书包
scene: 班里的辩论赛上，大家分析利弊。The biggest disadvantage of walking to school is getting wet on rainy days.
sceneCN: 这里 disadvantage 是「不利条件」（第 1 个义项：不好的方面）；句意是步行上学最大的坏处是雨天会淋湿。

derivatives.zh: disadvantage 的词基，义为「优势；有利条件」
过去分词作形容词，义为「处于不利地位的」
advantage 加后缀构成，义为「有利的」

senses.title: An unfavourable condition
senses.definition: something that makes success less likely
senses.definitionCN: 使成功可能性降低的因素
senses.example: Not having a computer at home is a disadvantage for the online class.
senses.exampleCN: 家里没有电脑，上网课就不方便，这是一种劣势。
senses.why: Advantage comes from ahead (abante); dis- turns it around, so disadvantage is being held back.
senses.whyCN: advantage 本义「领先」，加 dis- 便成了「被拖后」。

senses.title: A fault or a problem
senses.definition: a bad point of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物不好的一面
senses.example: Every plan has disadvantages, so we must compare them first.
senses.exampleCN: 每个方案都有缺点，所以要先作比较。
senses.why: What holds one back is also a fault of the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 拖人后腿的因素同时也是事物自身的毛病。

intro.en: Disadvantage is advantage wearing the prefix dis-.
intro.cn: disadvantage 是 advantage 加上前缀 dis-。

items.en: Old French avant meant before or ahead, from Latin abante.
items.cn: 古法语 avant 意为在前面，出自拉丁语 abante。

items.en: English built advantage, meaning a position ahead of others.
items.cn: 中古英语构成 advantage，指领先的地位。

items.en: The prefix dis- (against, apart) made disadvantage in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪加上 dis-（相反、分离）构成 disadvantage。

items.en: It named both bad conditions in life and faults of things.
items.cn: 它既指生活中的不利境况，也指事物的缺陷。

items.en: School essays often ask for the advantages and disadvantages of a plan.
items.cn: 学校作文常要求分析某个方案的利与弊。

note.en: These words stand in the better-or-worse field.
note.cn: 这些词属于优劣比较义场。

entries.definitionCN: 形容词：处于不利地位的

normalIntro.en: Compare the two sides: dis-advantage vs advantage.
normalIntro.cn: 对照两侧：dis-advantage（劣势）与 advantage（优势）。

normal.en: disadvantage = dis + advantage, the opposite of advantage.
normal.cn: disadvantage = dis + advantage，advantage 的反义。

normal.en: at a disadvantage means in a weaker position.
normal.cn: at a disadvantage 指处于劣势。

normal.en: essays often list advantages and disadvantages.
normal.cn: 作文常需列出利与弊。

normal.en: avant- inside means ahead, like in advance.
normal.cn: 词中的 avant- 表示「在前」，如 advance。

normal.en: a disadvantage is something that holds you back.
normal.cn: disadvantage 就是拖住你的东西。

abstract.en: Picture runners where one carries a heavy bag.
abstract.cn: 想象赛跑者中有一个背着沉重书包。

abstract.en: Feel the wind pushing you backwards.
abstract.cn: 体会逆风把你往后推的感觉。

abstract.en: See two lists on the blackboard: good and bad.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上的两栏清单：利与弊。

examples.en: A short ruler is a disadvantage when you draw a long line.
examples.cn: 画长线时，尺子太短是个不利条件。

examples.en: Living far from school puts me at a disadvantage in winter.
examples.cn: 冬天住得离学校远，我就处于不利地位。

examples.en: Let's list the advantages and disadvantages of the new timetable.
examples.cn: 我们来列一列新课程表的利与弊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弟斯 Advanced 得低」——弟弟没能领先（advance），处于劣势

root: 来自 disadvantage，dis-（相反）+ advantage（优势）；advantage 出自古法语 avantage，源于拉丁语 abante（在前面）。

sensesIntro.en: Disadvantage is the weaker side of a comparison.
sensesIntro.cn: disadvantage 指比较中的劣势一面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: running with a heavy bag
core.cn: 核心意象：背着沉重书包赛跑

From a person to a plan
branches.cn: 从人的处境到方案的毛病

latinIntro.en: Advantage traces to Latin abante, from before.

definition_zh: 不同意；意见不一致；有分歧
definition_en: to have a different opinion from someone
core_image: 两个人指着相反方向的箭头
scene: 小组讨论春游去哪，两个人意见不合。I disagree with Tom: the museum is better than the park.
sceneCN: 这里 disagree 是「不同意」（第 1 个义项：意见不同）；句意是我不同意汤姆的看法：博物馆比公园更好。

derivatives.zh: disagree 的词基，义为「同意」
disagree 加名词后缀构成，义为「分歧；争执」
agree 加名词后缀构成，义为「同意；协议」

senses.title: To have a different opinion
senses.definition: to have a different opinion from someone else
senses.definitionCN: 与别人看法不同
senses.example: Experts disagree about the best way to learn English.
senses.exampleCN: 专家们在学英语的最佳方法上意见不一。
senses.why: Agree comes from gratus (pleasing); dis- removes the pleasing, so disagree is to stop seeing eye to eye.
senses.whyCN: agree 出自 gratus（令人高兴的），加上 dis- 便失去了那份「合意」，即看法不再一致。

senses.title: To clash or not match
senses.definition: to be different from each other, or not to match
senses.definitionCN: 彼此不同或不相符
senses.example: The two reports disagree on the number of visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 两份报告在游客人数上不一致。
senses.why: When two accounts cannot please each other, they clash; the word moved from opinions to facts.
senses.whyCN: 两份说法无法「互相合意」，便相互冲突；词义从看法扩展到事实。

intro.en: Disagree is agree wearing the negative prefix dis-.
intro.cn: disagree 是 agree 加否定前缀 dis-。

items.en: Latin gratus meant pleasing or thankful, and gratum meant to please.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gratus 意为令人高兴的、感激的，动词 gratum 意为取悦。

items.en: Old French agreer meant to please or to accept willingly.
items.cn: 古法语 agreer 意为使高兴、欣然接受。

items.en: English borrowed agree in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语借入 agree。

items.en: The prefix dis- (apart, undo) built disagree soon after.
items.cn: 不久之后加上 dis-（分开、解除）构成 disagree。

items.en: Disagreement names the state, disagreeable the unpleasant manner.
items.cn: disagreement 指分歧状态，disagreeable 指令人不快的脾性。

note.en: These words share the agree root or the dis- prefix.
note.cn: 这些词同出 agree 词根，或带 dis- 前缀。

entries.definition: to say yes or share an opinion
to say no to a plan

normalIntro.en: Split it: dis- (apart) + agree (say yes).
normalIntro.cn: 拆开记忆：dis-（分开）+ agree（同意）。

normal.en: disagree = dis + agree, not agreeing.
normal.cn: disagree = dis + agree，不同意。

normal.en: disagree with sb is the classic pattern.
normal.cn: disagree with sb 是经典搭配。

normal.en: disagreement is the noun for the quarrel.
normal.cn: disagreement 是表示分歧的名词。

normal.en: agree to disagree means stop arguing politely.
normal.cn: agree to disagree 指友好地各自保留意见。

normal.en: grat- inside means pleasing, like grateful.
normal.cn: 词根 grat- 表示「令人高兴」，如 grateful。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows pointing opposite ways.
abstract.cn: 想象两支方向相反的箭头。

abstract.en: Hear two voices rising in a small meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象小型会议里两个渐渐提高的声音。

abstract.en: Feel the head shake left and right.
abstract.cn: 体会头左右摇动的动作。

examples.en: My sister and I often disagree about what to watch on TV.
examples.cn: 我和妹妹常常为看什么电视节目争论。

examples.en: Even good friends can disagree sometimes.
examples.cn: 即使是好朋友，有时也会有分歧。

examples.en: The two maps disagree about where the old temple is.
examples.cn: 两幅地图对古寺的位置说法不一。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弟斯额格力」——弟弟使劲额（n ê）着说「不格力」，不肯同意

root: 来自 disagree，dis-（分开、解除）+ agree（同意）；agree 出自古法语 agreer，源于拉丁语 gratus（令人高兴的）。

sensesIntro.en: Disagree first splits opinions, then facts.
sensesIntro.cn: disagree 先指看法分歧，再指事实不相符。

core.cn: 核心意象：两支相反的箭头

latinIntro.en: The agree root is Latin gratus, pleasing.

definition_zh: 消失；不见；不复存在
definition_en: to go away so that nobody can see or find it
core_image: 魔术师手中凭空消失的硬币
scene: 课间休息后，操场上的猫不见了。The little cat disappeared behind the wall in one second.
sceneCN: 这里 disappear 是「消失」（第 1 个义项：看不见了）；句意是小猫一秒钟就消失在墙后。

derivatives.zh: disappear 的词基，义为「出现」
appear 加名词后缀构成，义为「外貌；出现」
disappear 加名词后缀构成，义为「消失」

senses.title: To go out of sight
senses.definition: to go somewhere so that people cannot see it any more
senses.definitionCN: 走到人们看不见的地方
senses.example: The sun disappeared behind the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳躲到云后面去了。
senses.why: Appear means to come into view; dis- pushes it out of view again.
senses.whyCN: appear 意为「进入视野」，dis- 又把它推出视野。

senses.title: To stop existing
senses.definition: to stop existing or being used
senses.definitionCN: 不再存在或不再被使用
senses.example: Many old customs are slowly disappearing.
senses.exampleCN: 许多古老的习俗正在慢慢消失。
senses.why: When something leaves sight forever, it leaves the world too.
senses.whyCN: 当某物永远离开视线，它也离开了这个世界。

intro.en: Disappear is appear plus the prefix dis-.
intro.cn: disappear 是 appear 加前缀 dis-。

items.en: Latin apparere meant to come forth, built on ad- (toward) and parere (to show oneself).
items.cn: 拉丁语 apparere 意为出现，由 ad-（朝向）加 parere（显露自身）构成。

items.en: Old French apareir meant to appear or to be visible.
items.cn: 古法语 apareir 意为出现、可见。

items.en: English borrowed appear in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入 appear。

items.en: The prefix dis- made disappear in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪加上 dis- 构成 disappear。

items.en: Disappearance names the act; the word now also covers extinct animals and lost customs.
items.cn: disappearance 指消失这一行为；如今也用于灭绝的动物与失传的习俗。

note.en: These words share the appear root or the vanishing field.
note.cn: 这些词同出 appear 词根，或属于消失义场。

normalIntro.en: Split it: dis- (away) + appear (come into view).
normalIntro.cn: 拆开记忆：dis-（离开）+ appear（进入视野）。

normal.en: disappear = dis + appear, no longer seen.
normal.cn: disappear = dis + appear，不再被看见。

normal.en: appear is the opposite: to show up.
normal.cn: appear 是反义词：出现。

normal.en: disappear without a trace means nothing left behind.
normal.cn: disappear without a trace 指消失得无影无踪。

normal.en: disappearance is the noun form.
normal.cn: disappearance 是它的名词形式。

normal.en: par- inside means to show, like transparent.
normal.cn: 词根 par- 表示「显现」，如 transparent。

abstract.en: Picture a coin vanishing from an open palm.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币从摊开的手心里消失。

abstract.en: Watch fog eating the far end of the street.
abstract.cn: 看着雾吞掉街道的尽头。

abstract.en: Hear the last note fade into silence.
abstract.cn: 听最后一个音符淡入寂静。

examples.en: The magician made the rabbit disappear in his hat.
examples.cn: 魔术师让兔子在帽子里消失了。

examples.en: Dinosaurs disappeared from the earth long ago.
examples.cn: 恐龙很久以前就从地球上消失了。

examples.en: My pen disappeared again; maybe someone borrowed it.
examples.cn: 我的钢笔又不见了，也许是有人借走了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弟斯额皮尔」——弟弟一伸手，苹果（apple）皮儿立刻消失

root: 来自 disappear，dis-（离开、解除）+ appear（出现）；appear 出自古法语 apareir，源于拉丁语 apparere（显现）。

sensesIntro.en: Disappear pushes things out of sight, then out of the world.
sensesIntro.cn: disappear 先让事物离开视线，再让它不复存在。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin vanishing from a palm
core.cn: 核心意象：手心里凭空消失的硬币

branches.cn: 从一时不见到永远消失
渐渐消逝的习俗与动物

intro.en: Disappear = dis- + appear, fully transparent.

latinIntro.en: The appear root is Latin parere, to show oneself.
latinIntro.cn: appear 的词根是拉丁语 parere（显现自身）。

definition_zh: 使失望；使落空；辜负（期望）
definition_en: to make someone sad because something hoped for did not happen
core_image: 孩子眼里的气球慢慢瘪了下去
scene: 运动会上，接力赛只拿了第四名。The result disappointed us, but our teacher cheered us up.
sceneCN: 这里 disappoint 是「使失望」（第 1 个义项：让盼望落空）；句意是这个结果让我们失望，但老师鼓励了我们。

derivatives.zh: 过去分词作形容词，义为「感到失望的」
现在分词作形容词，义为「令人失望的」
disappoint 加名词后缀构成，义为「失望；令人失望的事」
同根词，义为「任命」

senses.title: To let hopes fall
senses.definition: to make someone sad because a hope or plan fails
senses.definitionCN: 因希望或计划落空而让人难过
senses.example: The rain disappointed our plan for a picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 下雨让我们的野餐计划泡汤了。
senses.why: To appoint was to arrange or fix a thing in place; dis- undoes the arrangement, and the hope falls flat.
senses.whyCN: appoint 本义是「安排妥当」，dis- 解除了这种安排，希望随之落空。

senses.title: To fail to meet expectations
senses.definition: to be worse than someone expected
senses.definitionCN: 比预期差
senses.example: The film promised much but disappointed its fans.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影预告很吸引人，却让影迷失望。

intro.en: Dishonest is honest wearing the negative dis-.

items.en: Old French honeste meant honourable and decent.

items.en: English borrowed honest in the thirteenth century.

items.en: The prefix dis- built dishonest soon after.
items.cn: 此后加 dis- 构成 dishonest。

items.en: Dishonesty names the behaviour, dishonest the person.
